newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: WHO doctor jets into S.Africa after Ebola outbreak.
newsitem.headline: WHO doctor jets into S.Africa after Ebola outbreak.

text.p: A World Health Organisation (WHO) official jetted into Johannesburg on Sunday to review the first outbreak of Ebola fever inside South Africa, local health officials said.

WHO doctor Brian Gushulak, chairman of a working group tasked with revising international health regulations for cross-border movement of people and goods, met the Gauteng province's Ebola task team after his arrival for a 3-day trip.

He was quoted by health officials as saying the essential responses of infection control, surveillance and monitoring of contacts and counselling were correctly in place. "I am confident that the situation is under control," he added.
Marilyn Lahana, a 46-year-old mother of two who nursed a Gabon doctor and contracted Ebola from him, is critically ill with multiple organ dysfunction and is dependent on life support systems.
Doctors treating Lahana, the first person to contract Ebola inside the country, said she had experienced bleeding on the brain on Friday. They were unable to say if she had sustained brain damage.
Without early treatment, Ebola, which killed 245 people in Zaire last year and 35 people in two outbreaks in Gabon earlier this year, is fatal in 80 to 90 percent of cases.
With early diagnosis, the fatality rate can be lowered to around 30 percent, South African doctors said.
